title: Feature: Global workspace sync for multi-monitor setups
head: d53f6f8e16e8
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Turning global mode off hides occupied second-monitor slots and number keys jump to a different monitor
leads.consequence: Example: after using global slot 2 on a base-10 monitor, occupied workspace 12 remains. Disabling only removes the toggle file; local-mode slotOfId(12) is 12 and workspaceIds excludes it, while Super+2 dispatches raw workspace 2 on the base-0 display. The bar cannot show or click the occupied workspace. It remains in compositor history and can still be recovered by other navigation or switching global back on; it is not deleted. Migrate occupied workspaces or preserve access to IDs above 10 until moved, including when disabling the toggle.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1: behaviour is inherent to local mode for ids above 10, at most a doc note; not published

leads.summary: Opening the keybindings menu inside Hyprland starts the global workspace setup job
leads.consequence: The source-scanning menu replays ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua under a stub hl environment, but inherits HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE from a real desktop invocation. The gate sees a session, load_bases reads real state, hl.get_monitors returns an empty stub proxy, and the unconditional os.execute at line 197 backgrounds omarchy-ensure-workspaces on the real session every time the menu scans the bindings. If any slot is missing the delayed job changes workspace focus and restores by active ID; otherwise it still launches an unnecessary subprocess and live IPC. Gate on real hl capability and avoid real setup/jobs during introspection; add a menu test retaining a signature.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus hypothesis H1 (pre-existing, probably harmless); not published

leads.summary: Enabling global mode silently replaces a user-defined former-workspace binding
leads.consequence: Users are told to put custom o.rebind or hl.unbind in ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua; config/hypr/hyprland.lua loads that at line 21 before toggles at line 26. This toggle calls o.rebind(SUPER+CTRL+TAB), which unbinds the user's custom mapping and installs previous_per_monitor. It also adds that key when omarchy_default_bindings=false. Preserve user override/disabled bindings, or make the mode-aware default binding at the same precedence as other packaged defaults.

leads.summary: Two quick toggle changes can leave the workspace bar in the wrong mode
leads.consequence: FileView starts a bash probe whenever the directory changes by setting Process.running=true; Quickshell's Process::startProcessIfReady returns immediately if a probe is already running and does not queue a second run. A flag change while the previous probe runs can be missed, and its older result overwrites globalModeActive. Bar then renders/clicks according to stale mode (raw workspace N versus mode-aware global wrapper) until another directory event or restart. Debounce or queue an after-finish recheck, or use the toggle command to nudge an explicit IPC refresh. Adjacent Bar.qml:1181-1193 documents this watcher problem and already has an IPC recovery path.

leads.summary: Unresolved focused monitor can silently move a window onto the wrong monitor
leads.consequence: On a monitor with base 10 or higher, a failing or malformed hyprctl monitors query, or a newly connected monitor not in the persisted map, falls back to raw workspace N, which can already belong to the base-0 monitor. The move is silent (follow=false), so the window disappears from the current display rather than reaching slot N on the user's monitor, with exit 0 when dispatch succeeds. Query or allocate this monitor's base, otherwise fail visibly rather than dispatch an unrelated monitor's workspace. The existing test explicitly asserts the raw-slot fallback as intended but does not assert monitor ownership.
leads.triage: intended fallback restored after R3; dropped

leads.summary: Unrelated positive workspace IDs are misrepresented as global slots in the bar
leads.consequence: With one monitor assigned base 0, a preexisting or user-created workspace 42 is not part of the configured 1-10 slots, but slotOfId(42) returns 2 because the initial bound is 99; if it has windows the bar displays slot 2 as occupied. Clicking slot 2 goes to workspace 2 instead of 42. Unlike Lua slot_of which checks actual base ranges, QML checks only a high-water mark. Read the bases map or Hyprland's per-monitor workspace rules and classify only allocated IDs.

leads.summary: Delayed workspace-creation helper still runs after global mode has been switched off
leads.consequence: The toggle removes only workspace-global.lua but intentionally keeps monitor-bases.json. An already spawned ensure job sleeps for one second; after the user disables the mode it checks bases and signature but not the toggle, and if high-numbered workspaces are missing it dispatches to recreate them, temporarily stealing focus and leaving global-range workspaces in local mode. Before dispatch, check the mode flag and ideally cancel pending jobs on off. Update the ensure fixture to create the enabled flag for its existing positive cases, then add an off-transition case; today it creates only the bases file.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1 reproduced that the script ignores the flag, very low transient effect; not published

leads.summary: On a monitors query failure the global switch dispatches saved disconnected outputs
leads.consequence: A failed or malformed hyprctl monitors -j makes live_monitors=None, explicitly turning off the connected-monitor filter. Every disconnected saved monitor then gets a workspace focus dispatch, which can create its workspace on a connected monitor and change focus; the command can return 0 if the dispatches themselves succeed. Keep the current monitor untouched on query failure, or fail and retry after live output names are available. This is the opposite of ensure-workspaces which fails closed on the same input.
leads.triage: fallback verified as intended in R5; dropped

leads.summary: The Python sync writer truncates the shared bases map despite Lua's stated atomic-write premise
leads.consequence: The Lua comment says both writers use temp-file/rename, but Python opens the live file with 'w' and dumps JSON in place. A concurrent read from Lua's load_bases during this short write sees an empty/partial object and can allocate base 0 anew; a simultaneous sync or hotplug can overwrite saved assignments. If the timing is possible during live event scheduling, windows in disconnected saved ranges become mislabelled or the file is briefly unparseable to switch helpers. Make Python write an fsynced temp + os.replace under a shared lock and test concurrent readers.

leads.summary: Open numpad-workspace PR #12566 overlaps all three new mode-aware bindings
leads.consequence: #12566 adds secondary numpad keycodes in the same loop but binds raw hl.dsp.focus/hl.dsp.window.move. On the divergent heads, git merge-file produced conflict markers at upstream/merged-12566/merged:23-38; GitHub reports #12566 MERGEABLE against master, not against this PR. Naively retaining both sets makes the new numpad shortcuts ignore global mode and send windows to raw slots. Coordinate the resolution so both key families call the mode-aware wrappers; run the merged bindings fixture after resolving the conflict.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator merge-tree in disposable clone (conflict in tiling.lua); published in Details

leads.summary: Open per-monitor bar PR #13369 cannot interpret this PR's second-monitor workspace IDs
leads.consequence: #13369's WorkspacesModel accepts only rules and live IDs 1..10 (diff lines 145-154,190-195), while this PR reserves 11..20 for its second monitor. Their Workspaces.qml changes overlap in multiple merge conflict blocks at upstream/merged-13369/merged:18-109 and onward, despite #13369 being MERGEABLE against master and not stacked. Resolving by keeping that model without adapting it makes the second monitor's 11-20 workspace slots disappear from its bar. Reconcile slot-to-ID conversion and per-monitor presentation explicitly when merging; neither PR's tests have run on an unresolved merge.
leads.triage: factual; verified (conflict in Workspaces.qml); published in Details

leads.summary: The existing Toggle menu offers workspace-layout controls but not the new global mode
leads.consequence: The new file is opt-in via omarchy-hyprland-toggle workspace-global, yet the shipped Toggle menu lists Workspace Layout, Window Gaps and 1-Window Ratio without it. Users following the menu cannot turn global sync on or off and will not discover its existence there. Register a Workspace Global action pointing to the existing toggle command (with user-facing explanation of the mode change).
leads.triage: factual (no menu entry) but product choice, pre-existing; not published

leads.summary: Document the opt-in global mode and switching it off in the monitor/workspace guide
leads.consequence: The monitor guide documents per-monitor workspace rules but not the new opt-in global toggle; manual/07-hotkeys.md describes the same shortcuts with no mode distinction, and docs/file-layout.md:116-117 lists the packaged Hyprland toggles without workspace-global. The menu has no entry either, leaving no shipped discoverable enable or recovery procedure. Add the exact omarchy hyprland toggle workspace-global on/off commands to the monitor guide and describe local/global keyboard, bar, and cleanup semantics.

leads.summary: A failed workspaces query is mistaken for all workspaces missing
leads.consequence: If hyprctl workspaces -j exits nonzero, the helper leaves existing_ids as an empty set instead of failing closed. For every connected monitor in the saved map it then dispatches all 10 workspace IDs, potentially changing focus up to ten times per display before attempting to restore the old ID. The command still exits 0 and the next run repeats while the query fails. Handle nonzero workspaces query like the monitors query at lines 48-57, and include a failing-workspaces fixture.

limits: No desktop/Omadev slot was reserved. Source confirms the command paths and Quickshell v0.3.1 timing, but exact on-screen timing after a rapid toggle was not reproduced natively; Quickshell package version may differ from sampled tag.

Non-atomic writer interleaving is a hypothesis: a concurrent hotplug/sync trace or an isolated fixture forcing an open-read in the write window would settle whether real scheduling exposes it; no such run was performed.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** at `d53f6f8e16e8`, the three open findings from [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5864691725) are fixed, but enabling global mode now overrides a personal SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding.

- **Resolved:** `move-window-to-aw-test.sh` (10/10), SUPER+CTRL+TAB in local mode (`previous` again), the 241 root files.
- **Still present:** the optional switch-test filter note.

### Global mode overrides a personal SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding

The new `o.rebind` at the end of `workspace-global.lua` runs after the user's `hypr/bindings.lua`, because `hyprland.lua` loads toggles last. **Impact:** with the toggle on, a personal rebind or unbind of that key becomes `previous_per_monitor`, although the config says personal overrides replace Omarchy's defaults.

**Suggested change:** choose the selector in `tiling.lua` from the toggle's flag file and drop the rebind.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at d53f6f8e16e8)</summary>

# Reproducer: the workspace-global toggle replaces a user's own SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding

Reviewed head: `d53f6f8e16e8` (omacom/omarchy#12978). Control: `d8990d9f15f7` (previous review) and a diagnostic copy of the head with the suggested change.

`config/hypr/hyprland.lua` loads Omarchy's default bindings, then the user's `hypr/bindings.lua`, then `default.hypr.toggles`. The new `o.rebind` at the end of `default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua` therefore runs after the user's overrides and replaces any SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding the user set there.

The test below evaluates the shipped `config/hypr/hyprland.lua` entry point in a scratch HOME (user config copied from `config/hypr/`, toggle copied the way `omarchy-hyprland-toggle on` does it) under a stub `hl`. The stub's `unbind` removes binds by display key, exact or whitespace-stripped and lower-cased, as `CKeybindManager::removeKeybind(const std::string&)` does in Hyprland 0.56.2. `os.execute` is stubbed and `io.popen` only runs `require_all`'s `find`, so no helper command starts.

Save as `test/shell.d/workspace-global-user-binding-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/workspace-global-user-binding-test.sh` from the repository root. It needs `lua`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Enabling workspace-global must not replace a SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding the user
# set in ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua ("Put your personal overrides in these
# files. They're loaded after Omarchy's defaults" - config/hypr/hyprland.lua).
#
# Evaluates the shipped ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua entry point in a scratch
# HOME, with the toggle copied the way omarchy-hyprland-toggle does it, under
# a stub hl whose unbind() removes binds by display key like Hyprland does.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command lua

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# setup_home HOME on|off
setup_home() {
  local home="$1" global="$2"
  mkdir -p "$home/.config/hypr" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr"
  cp "$ROOT"/config/hypr/*.lua "$home/.config/hypr/"
  cp "$ROOT/default/hypr/toggles/flags.lua" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/"
  if [[ $global == "on" ]]; then
    cp "$ROOT/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/"
  fi
}

# Print every final SUPER+CTRL+TAB bind as: keys<TAB>description<TAB>dispatcher(arg)
ctrl_tab_binds() {
  local home="$1"
  HOME="$home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$home/.config" XDG_STATE_HOME="$home/.local/state" \
    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=test lua <<'LUA'
local binds = {}

local function normalize(keys)
  return (keys:gsub("%s", "")):lower()
end

local function render(value)
  if type(value) ~= "table" then
    return string.format("%q", tostring(value))
  end
  local keys = {}
  for key in pairs(value) do keys[#keys + 1] = tostring(key) end
  table.sort(keys)
  local parts = {}
  for _, key in ipairs(keys) do parts[#parts + 1] = key .. " = " .. render(value[key]) end
  return "{ " .. table.concat(parts, ", ") .. " }"
end

local function dispatcher(path)
  return setmetatable({}, {
    __index = function(_, key) return dispatcher(path .. "." .. key) end,
    __call = function(_, arg) return { path = path, arg = arg } end,
  })
end

hl = setmetatable({
  dsp = dispatcher("hl.dsp"),
  bind = function(keys, action, opts)
    binds[#binds + 1] = { keys = keys, action = action, description = opts and opts.description }
    return {}
  end,
  -- Hyprland 0.56.2 CKeybindManager::removeKeybind(displayKeys): exact or
  -- whitespace-stripped, lower-cased display key match.
  unbind = function(keys)
    for index = #binds, 1, -1 do
      if binds[index].keys == keys or normalize(binds[index].keys) == normalize(keys) then
        table.remove(binds, index)
      end
    end
  end,
  get_monitors = function() return {} end,
  get_config = function() return nil end,
}, {
  -- Any other hl.* call returns a plain table, as in hyprland-binding-conflicts-test.sh.
  __index = function() return function() return {} end end,
})

-- Never start helper commands from a test; allow only require_all's find.
os.execute = function() return true end
local real_popen = io.popen
io.popen = function(command, mode)
  if command:sub(1, 5) == "find " then return real_popen(command, mode) end
  return real_popen("true", mode)
end

local ok, err = pcall(dofile, os.getenv("HOME") .. "/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua")
if not ok then
  io.stderr:write("config load failed: " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
  os.exit(2)
end

for _, bind in ipairs(binds) do
  if normalize(bind.keys) == normalize("SUPER + CTRL + TAB") then
    local action = bind.action
    local rendered = type(action) == "table" and action.path and (action.path .. "(" .. render(action.arg) .. ")") or render(action)
    print(bind.keys .. "\t" .. tostring(bind.description) .. "\t" .. rendered)
  end
end
LUA
}

# A personal override, written the way config/hypr/bindings.lua documents it.
user_override='o.rebind("SUPER + CTRL + TAB", "Focus next monitor", hl.dsp.focus({ monitor = "+1" }))'

# ── Control: toggle off keeps the user's binding ─────────────────────────────
setup_home "$tmp/local" off
printf '\n%s\n' "$user_override" >>"$tmp/local/.config/hypr/bindings.lua"
output=$(ctrl_tab_binds "$tmp/local")
[[ $output == $'SUPER + CTRL + TAB\tFocus next monitor\thl.dsp.focus({ monitor = "+1" })' ]] ||
  fail "toggle off: the user's SUPER+CTRL+TAB override is the only binding" "got: $output"
pass "toggle off: the user's SUPER+CTRL+TAB override is the only binding"

# ── Toggle on must keep it too ────────────────────────────────────────────────
setup_home "$tmp/global" on
printf '\n%s\n' "$user_override" >>"$tmp/global/.config/hypr/bindings.lua"
output=$(ctrl_tab_binds "$tmp/global")
[[ $output == $'SUPER + CTRL + TAB\tFocus next monitor\thl.dsp.focus({ monitor = "+1" })' ]] ||
  fail "toggle on: the user's SUPER+CTRL+TAB override survives" "got: $output"
pass "toggle on: the user's SUPER+CTRL+TAB override survives"
```

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### Fixes to the toggle module do not reach users who already enabled it

`omarchy-hyprland-toggle` copies the whole 320-line module into `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/`, and Hyprland loads that copy. # Supporting test (optional test improvement): SUPER+CTRL+TAB in both modes

Reviewed head: `d53f6f8e16e8` (omacom/omarchy#12978). No test in the PR checks SUPER+CTRL+TAB, so neither the local-mode change reviewed at `d8990d9f15f7` nor the current global-mode rebind is covered. This test evaluates the shipped `config/hypr/hyprland.lua` entry point in a scratch HOME with the toggle off and on, and asserts the single final SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding: `previous` with the toggle off, `previous_per_monitor` with it on.

Save as `test/shell.d/workspace-global-ctrl-tab-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/workspace-global-ctrl-tab-test.sh`. It needs `lua`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# SUPER+CTRL+TAB ("Former workspace") must keep Hyprland's global history
# ("previous") in local mode and use the focused monitor's history
# ("previous_per_monitor") while workspace-global is enabled.
#
# Evaluates the shipped ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua entry point in a scratch
# HOME, with the toggle copied the way omarchy-hyprland-toggle does it, under
# a stub hl whose unbind() removes binds by display key like Hyprland does.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command lua

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# setup_home HOME on|off
setup_home() {
  local home="$1" global="$2"
  mkdir -p "$home/.config/hypr" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr"
  cp "$ROOT"/config/hypr/*.lua "$home/.config/hypr/"
  cp "$ROOT/default/hypr/toggles/flags.lua" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/"
  if [[ $global == "on" ]]; then
    cp "$ROOT/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua" "$home/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/"
  fi
}

# Print every final SUPER+CTRL+TAB bind as: keys<TAB>description<TAB>dispatcher(arg)
ctrl_tab_binds() {
  local home="$1"
  HOME="$home" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$home/.config" XDG_STATE_HOME="$home/.local/state" \
    OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE=test lua <<'LUA'
local binds = {}

local function normalize(keys)
  return (keys:gsub("%s", "")):lower()
end

local function render(value)
  if type(value) ~= "table" then
    return string.format("%q", tostring(value))
  end
  local keys = {}
  for key in pairs(value) do keys[#keys + 1] = tostring(key) end
  table.sort(keys)
  local parts = {}
  for _, key in ipairs(keys) do parts[#parts + 1] = key .. " = " .. render(value[key]) end
  return "{ " .. table.concat(parts, ", ") .. " }"
end

local function dispatcher(path)
  return setmetatable({}, {
    __index = function(_, key) return dispatcher(path .. "." .. key) end,
    __call = function(_, arg) return { path = path, arg = arg } end,
  })
end

hl = setmetatable({
  dsp = dispatcher("hl.dsp"),
  bind = function(keys, action, opts)
    binds[#binds + 1] = { keys = keys, action = action, description = opts and opts.description }
    return {}
  end,
  -- Hyprland 0.56.2 CKeybindManager::removeKeybind(displayKeys): exact or
  -- whitespace-stripped, lower-cased display key match.
  unbind = function(keys)
    for index = #binds, 1, -1 do
      if binds[index].keys == keys or normalize(binds[index].keys) == normalize(keys) then
        table.remove(binds, index)
      end
    end
  end,
  get_monitors = function() return {} end,
  get_config = function() return nil end,
}, {
  -- Any other hl.* call returns a plain table, as in hyprland-binding-conflicts-test.sh.
  __index = function() return function() return {} end end,
})

-- Never start helper commands from a test; allow only require_all's find.
os.execute = function() return true end
local real_popen = io.popen
io.popen = function(command, mode)
  if command:sub(1, 5) == "find " then return real_popen(command, mode) end
  return real_popen("true", mode)
end

local ok, err = pcall(dofile, os.getenv("HOME") .. "/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua")
if not ok then
  io.stderr:write("config load failed: " .. tostring(err) .. "\n")
  os.exit(2)
end

for _, bind in ipairs(binds) do
  if normalize(bind.keys) == normalize("SUPER + CTRL + TAB") then
    local action = bind.action
    local rendered = type(action) == "table" and action.path and (action.path .. "(" .. render(action.arg) .. ")") or render(action)
    print(bind.keys .. "\t" .. tostring(bind.description) .. "\t" .. rendered)
  end
end
LUA
}

# ── Local mode (toggle off) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
setup_home "$tmp/local" off
output=$(ctrl_tab_binds "$tmp/local")
(( $(grep -c . <<<"$output") == 1 )) || fail "local mode has one SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding" "got: $output"
[[ $output == *'workspace = "previous" }'* ]] ||
  fail "local mode: SUPER+CTRL+TAB uses Hyprland's global history (previous)" "got: $output"
pass "local mode: SUPER+CTRL+TAB jumps to the former workspace across monitors (previous)"

# ── Global mode (toggle on) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
setup_home "$tmp/global" on
output=$(ctrl_tab_binds "$tmp/global")
(( $(grep -c . <<<"$output") == 1 )) || fail "global mode has one SUPER+CTRL+TAB binding" "got: $output"
[[ $output == *'workspace = "previous_per_monitor" }'* ]] ||
  fail "global mode: SUPER+CTRL+TAB uses the focused monitor's history (previous_per_monitor)" "got: $output"
pass "global mode: SUPER+CTRL+TAB stays on the focused monitor's history (previous_per_monitor)"
```
